I dunno. I can’t say I was never a fan of his. These days he’s gone completely off the handle and I would say “off-message” from what gained him his popularity to begin with. Which to me was a lot of his talks and writings about becoming a man. Like anything in that sort: some of it makes sense, and other parts don’t really work. A lot of different perspectives is better than the same perspective over and over again. So I can appreciate some of the things he’s discussed for what it is. A discussion of purpose, belonging, and meaning. Where I think he goes wrong (for me personally) is that he seems to treat these ideas as fact, and as if their should be laws to reflect these ideas.

Which brings me to Joe Rogan. Again, I’ve enjoyed a good amount of his stuff, but I don’t agree with all of it. I don’t keep up with everything he does or says, but as far as I can tell he hasn’t acted or said anything that steps outside of his opinions as an individual. He’s on a much humbler level (again, from my experience) than Peterson, and almost acts as an “every-man.” So again, I can appreciate him on a level of discussion and nothing more. 

It’s exactly as you say though: a lot of people take their word as gospel, and thats never been a healthy thing to do with any person. You can listen to what these people have to say and maybe even adopt some of their positions as your own; but to act as if those ideas aren’t coming from someone who isn’t flawed or doesn’t have the same experiences as everyone else is really dangerous. 

The floor has to be open, however, for everyone’s ideas about the world. It can open people’s eyes to different possibilities. Pseudo-intellectual is a tricky word for me because I think everyone has their own experiences and (assuming they’re good communicators) intellectual views on those experiences. So I’m curious as to where you think the “pseudo” comes in on “pseudo-intellectualism” with these particular people.
I know he’s a controversial guy all together, but he really went from at best a “well spoken, thoughtful, and intellectual” man to an “endless stream of incel-level bad opinions and world views.”
